basis: Developmental and learning impairment define the syndrome; skeletal deformities and night blindness each annotated 30-79%. Asthma is a separate disease.
Developmental delay and intellectual impairment are core features; variable cardiac, urinary and skeletal anomalies lack evidence of >=30% frequency.
Mosquito-borne viral infection directly inflames the brain; gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish gastrointestinal injury.
Inherited cone dysfunction causes absent color vision and reduced visual acuity, with retinal abnormalities.
Glutaminase deficiency causes disordered glutamine metabolism with developmental delay and progressive cerebellar ataxia in 3/3 patients.
Skull ossification defects occur in 80-99%; eye malformations/cataracts and cleft palate/omphalocele each occur in 30-79%. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Carcinoma originates in a major salivary gland, usually the parotid; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Congenital muscular dystrophy, brain malformations and retinal dystrophy define this subtype; all three systems are affected in the reported patients.
Salmonella infection directly causes intestinal inflammation; systemic complications are not defining or sufficiently common.
Craniosynostosis, limb skeletal defects and congenital heart defects define the syndrome; respiratory infections do not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Direct lesion of the ulnar peripheral nerve; weakness does not independently establish skeletal muscle disease.
Immune-mediated granulomatous nervous system disease; pulmonary sarcoid involvement accompanies neurosarcoidosis in roughly 50-70%, although isolated neurologic disease occurs.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, documented in 15/15 patients; no additional organ disease is established.
Tumor originates in reproductive testicular tissue; no endocrine dysfunction or other qualifying organ involvement is intrinsic to this histologic subtype.
Congenital abnormal motor pathway development causes mirror movements and/or corpus callosum agenesis.
Inherited folate transport disorder defined by folate-responsive megaloblastic anemia and immunodeficiency.
Anorectal inflammation is usually infectious or associated with immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease per the definition; radiation-related forms are exceptions.
Inherited mitochondrial complex I deficiency manifests as optic neuropathy; visual loss and optic atrophy occur in 3/3 patients. Optic nerve involvement is ocular.
Limb reduction defects and cardiac anomalies define the syndrome; respiratory insufficiency lacks evidence of direct pulmonary pathology.
Intellectual developmental disorder with defining distal skeletal defects; common myokymia and hyporeflexia reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Gonococcal infection of the epididymis and testis; reproductive inflammation does not establish endocrine gonadal dysfunction.
Umbrella category explicitly defined by neurologic dysfunction of voluntary or involuntary movement; no other organ is consistently affected.
Isolated failure of sperm production causes male infertility; reproductive function alone has no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Inborn defect of ketone utilization and isoleucine catabolism causes ketoacidosis; acute altered consciousness is common, but lasting neurologic injury is under 30%.
Partial gonadal dysgenesis disrupts testicular endocrine development; congenital heart disease is a named feature, with tetralogy of Fallot in 1/3 patients.
